---
title: "Transcription shared across your devices"
date: 2026-11-27
lang: en
---

The idea (user, 2026-11-27): with several devices on one account, choose which ones
transcribe. The mini PC at home is always on and has a local model (superwhisper or
whisper.cpp): it transcribes every voice message the account receives, and the phone
shows the words without running a model. Settings → voice messages becomes one setting
for the account, showing which devices transcribe. And an account that lives only on a
phone needs an answer too: no transcription, a model on the phone, or a cloud service.

What holds today (0.5.2): each device transcribes on its own, only the open
conversation, with superwhisper (when it works offline) or whisper.cpp. Text and
subtitles stay in that device's cache, keyed by the file's id. That id comes from the
conversation's commit (`fileId`), so it is **the same on every device**: a transcript
made on one device fits the message on all of them. Joma already talks to its own
other devices with account messages to its own Jami ID (folder sync does, D-23).

Two facts shape the design. libjami's public API sends only plain text into a
conversation, no custom message types. And Jami keeps account messages for an offline
device only a short while, so a phone that was off for a day would miss them.

Sketch:

- **A private Joma conversation.** Joma creates one conversation per account with only
  you in it ("Joma"); Jami syncs it to all your devices, the phone included, and keeps
  its history. Transcripts go there as records: one line of text that starts with a
  marker and carries JSON (`joma:transcript {"file": …, "conv": …, "lang": "it",
  "text": …, "cues": …, "by": "minis"}`). Joma reads them and hides the conversation.
  It is end-to-end encrypted like any conversation, and only your devices are in it.
- **A live nudge.** The transcriber also sends an account message to your own ID, so a
  device that is on shows the words at once instead of at the next conversation sync.
- **Roles.** Each Joma device writes a device record in the same conversation: its
  name, the engines it has (superwhisper offline, whisper.cpp, a cloud key), whether it
  is always on, and whether it transcribes. Settings → voice messages shows them all
  and lets you choose. Devices shows "transcribes" on those that do.
- **The transcriber.** A device that transcribes watches every conversation, downloads
  each new voice or video message, transcribes it and posts the record. With two
  transcribers, the second waits a little and skips messages that already have one.
- **Readers.** Every device, the phone too, reads the records and shows the words under
  the message and the subtitles on videos. A device that transcribes for itself only
  (today's behaviour) still works without the shared conversation.

Joma for Android needs a patch to read the records and to hide the Joma conversation;
until then the phone shows that conversation as plain text lines (they read as
`joma:transcript …`).

# 1. Where transcripts travel

The private Joma conversation (lasting, reaches the phone after being off) plus a live
account message (instant). Proposal: yes. The same conversation can later carry other
per-account Joma settings (synced folders, quick messages, favourites).

- [x] A:

# 2. Who sees them

Only your devices. A contact never sees your transcripts unless you send them. Proposal:
only yours by default; a later per-conversation switch "share transcripts here" posts
them into that conversation for everyone (useful in a group where nobody transcribes).

- [x] A:

# 3. Choosing the transcribers

Proposal: settings → voice messages lists your devices with what each can do
("minis · superwhisper offline · always on"), and a switch per device. Default: every
device with a local engine transcribes for itself; a device marked **for all my
devices** transcribes everything, and then the others stop doing it themselves (they
wait for its records, and fall back to themselves after a few minutes if none comes).

- [x] A:

# 4. What gets transcribed

Proposal: new voice and video messages in every conversation, up to 10 minutes long.
When a transcriber is switched on, it also does the last 7 days. Older messages: on
demand. The phone's "transcribe" button asks the transcriber (a request record), so a
phone can get any old message transcribed by the mini PC.

- [x] A: i don't think it's necessary to transcribe the last 7 days. it should only be on-demand if a transcriber becomes available and older messages are not trascribed, there should be an option, (Right click, long press, or an icon "cc") to transcribe or sub message. also for video messages, I would probably run the transcription in background but leave the subs options with a cc button to activate the overlay

# 5. An account only on a phone

No other device to do the work. Options, any mix:

- (a) **no transcription** (the default);
- (b) **a model on the phone**: whisper.cpp's small multilingual models (75 to 150 MB)
  run on a recent phone, slowly for long messages and with some battery;
- (c) **a cloud service with your own key**: OpenAI's or Groq's Whisper API (an
  OpenAI-style endpoint, so one setting serves several providers); the audio leaves the
  phone, which the setting says plainly;
- (d) **superwhisper's cloud**: superwhisper's account works inside its own app; I have
  not found a public API it offers to other apps. To check before promising it.

Proposal: (a) by default, (c) as an opt-in setting, (b) later. The same cloud option
can serve a desktop without a local model.

# 6. Language

Proposal: automatic everywhere (the engine decides), with an optional language per
contact for people who always speak one ("Marta: Italian"), stored in the Joma
conversation so every device uses it.

- [x] A:

# 7. Order of work

Proposal:

1. The Joma conversation and the record format (with a test between two linked test
   profiles).
2. Desktop as transcriber and reader: every conversation in the background, records,
   the live nudge, the settings page with device roles.
3. Requests ("transcribe this one") and the 7-day catch-up.
4. Joma for Android reads records and hides the conversation (A2 in the plan).
5. The cloud key option, then a model on the phone.

- [x] A: we skip 5. let's just use superwhisper on desktop

# 8. Commands

Proposal: `joma transcribe <conversation> <message>` (asks the transcriber or does it
here), `joma transcription` (the devices and their roles, `--json`), `joma
transcription on|off|all` (this device's role).

- [x] A:

## Built (2026-11-28, 0.5.3.dev5)

From the answers: no 7-day catch-up, only new messages by themselves, older ones with
**cc** (and video subtitles behind cc); the sender's transcript travels with the voice
message as a reply that starts with 📝 (readable in every Jami app; Joma folds it under
the message), on by default; a device set to **for all my devices** transcribes every
conversation's new messages, attaches transcripts to your own messages (also those sent
from the phone) and brings the others' words to your devices that are on (an account
message). Not built yet: the private Joma conversation that keeps transcripts for
devices that were off (question 1), the device records and their list in settings
(question 3), the phone reading them (Android). Step 5 (cloud key, model on the phone)
is skipped, as answered; superwhisper stays the desktop's engine.
